tags.name: The Wall
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-07-09. Re-pulled all three sources directly. Depth 55-56m range reconfirmed (Seahawks: 10.2-55m; Dive Andaman: 10-56m; Barefoot: 10-55m). 200m+ length and dual-reef structure reconfirmed. Marine life (Napoleon wrasse, groupers, trevally, barracuda, snapper, bannerfish, octopus, marble rays, scorpionfish, stonefish) reconfirmed across all three sources. No factual changes required.

tags.name: MV Mars
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-07-09. scubalov.in reconfirmed depth 15m (10-16m range), storm cause, upright orientation, wooden cargo vessel type. travelsetu.com now states approximately 20m depth (the 2026-06-08 audit recorded this source as saying 30m -- figure appears to have changed or was misread previously; still conflicts with scubalov.in's more detailed 15m figure, which is retained as primary since scubalov.in is a dedicated dive-site listing with more specific detail). The 'April 2006' sinking date: only 'April' (no year) is corroborated by the primary source (scubalov.in); the year 2006 is sourced only to travelsetu.com, a general blog aggregator whose other claims conflict with primary sources -- year should be treated as unconfirmed. andamantourism.org gives no specific depth or date. No length, tonnage, or build date found for this vessel in any source across this or the prior audit -- likely undocumented, consistent with a small local wooden craft rather than a registered merchant vessel.

tags.name: South Button
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-07-09. Re-pulled all three sources directly. touristinindia.com and andamanislands.com reconfirm reef sharks, manta/devil rays, sea turtles, and the 5 sq km smallest-national-park status; wikipedia.org reconfirms park details and adds dugongs, dolphins as regionally documented fauna. REMOVED unconfirmed leopard shark claim carried over from the 2026-06-08 audit -- a fresh direct re-fetch of touristinindia.com found no mention of leopard or zebra sharks anywhere on the page; only generic 'reef sharks' is source-confirmed at this specific site. The prior note claiming touristinindia.com 'specifically records' leopard shark sightings could not be reproduced and appears to have been in error.

tags.name: Duncan's Wreck
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-07-09. All three sources re-pulled directly. Build 1923 by John Priestman & Co., Sunderland; dimensions 111m x 16m x 8m; sinking 2 March 1955 near Duncan Island in bad weather while carrying coal and timber from Calcutta to Bombay -- reconfirmed identically across all three sources (frogman.in, private-scuba.com, seahawksscuba.in). Tonnage 4,290 GRT remains single-sourced to private-scuba.com only; no primary maritime registry located to independently confirm -- caveat retained per wreck-history policy. Depth 18-22m (bow 5-10m, propeller ~18m) reconfirmed. Marine life reconfirmed. No changes required.

tags.name: Dixon's
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-07-09. Previous validation_source diveindia.com/2018/01/02/1st-dive-shop-in-the-andamans/ now returns HTTP 404 (dead link) -- replaced with scubadiving.com's 'How Three Brothers Put Havelock Island Diving on the Map' feature (Scuba Diving Magazine), which independently corroborates the 2006 discovery date, the anchor-slipping-deeper discovery story, the Poayesay family (Jackson, Dickson, Johnny), the Karen community background (Burmese group brought to the Andamans by the British in the 1920s-30s), and the DIVEIndia/Vandit Kalia connection (Kalia inherited equipment and the three divers from Herbert Burri's original Chidiya Tapu dive shop). Marine life expanded per frogman.in fresh re-fetch: added manta/mobula rays (frequent in peak season) and occasional whale sharks, both newly confirmed as site-specific. diveandaman.com and frogman.in reconfirm depth range 16-35m and pinnacle/cleaning-station structure.

tags.name: Lighthouse

tags.name: MV Primrose
tags.note: Re-audited 2026-07-09. Re-pulled NZ Herald and Wikipedia directly; UPI archive page returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch this pass (inaccessible to automated fetch, but headline and content corroborated via search index quotation, consistent with 2026-06-08 finding). Added South China Morning Post (scmp.com) as a fourth independent source, which resolves the crew-count question: SCMP states a '31-man total crew, including 21 Hong Kong sailors' -- confirming 31 as the correct total and clarifying that the '21' figure appearing in some coverage refers only to the Hong Kong-national subset, not a competing total headcount. This corroborates NZ Herald's 31 and reframes the UPI 'twenty-eight' figure as the remaining unresolved outlier (cause unknown; flagged, not guessed). Panamanian registration, 16,000-ton tonnage, 2 August 1981 grounding, chicken-feed-to-Australia cargo, ONGC helicopter rescue, and 1991 salvage/Sentinelese-arrowhead details all reconfirmed across sources. Captain name 'Liu Chunglong' remains single-sourced to NZ Herald; UPI independently describes him only as 'the Taiwanese captain' without naming him -- consistent, not contradictory, but not itself independent confirmation of the name.
